title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Night Prayer And The Transformations Of The Universe

questions.question: What happens in the sky when the time of ‘Isha begins?
questions.answer: The last light of day goes away, and night covers everything.

questions.question: What happens to the things people leave behind as time passes?
questions.answer: They fade away and are erased from this world.

questions.question: What does that fading away help a person remember?
questions.answer: That living things die and move on to another world.

questions.question: What does the passage say about this world compared with the hereafter?
questions.answer: This world is short and small, but the hereafter is lasting and great.

questions.question: Who is the only true One to love and worship?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: Why is Allah the only true One to worship, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because He easily changes night and day, seasons, and this world into the next.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah’s power over these changes?
questions.answer: It says He changes them easily, like turning pages.

questions.question: What main idea does this passage teach about the time of ‘Isha?
questions.answer: It reminds us of Allah’s power, the passing of this world, and the coming of the hereafter.

questions.question: At nightfall, what disappears from the horizon?
questions.answer: The last bits of daylight.

questions.question: After that, what covers the universe?
questions.answer: The world of night.

questions.question: What season is named as the cold white one?
questions.answer: Winter.

questions.question: What season is described as green and decorated?
questions.answer: Summer.

questions.question: When old signs of people’s work disappear over time, what does that make us think about?
questions.answer: Death and going to a different world.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to this short world?
questions.answer: It will be destroyed and come to an end.

questions.question: What kind of world opens after this one?
questions.answer: A wide, everlasting, majestic world.

questions.question: Which is stronger in the passage: people and things in the world, or Allah?
questions.answer: Allah is stronger than all of them.

questions.question: If Allah can change winter to spring, what else can He change?
questions.answer: He can change this world into the hereafter.

questions.question: What prayer time is this passage talking about?
questions.answer: The time of ‘Isha.

questions.question: What change happens first at that time?
questions.answer: Day ends and night begins.

questions.question: What does the change from day to night help us remember about the seasons?
questions.answer: It helps us remember summer changing into winter.

questions.question: What do disappearing traces from the past teach us?
questions.answer: Things in this world do not stay forever.

questions.question: Where do living things go after death, according to the passage?
questions.answer: To another world.

questions.question: How is this world described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is narrow, passing, and lowly.

questions.question: How is the hereafter described?
questions.answer: It is broad, eternal, and majestic.

questions.question: Why can only one Being be the real Owner and Ruler of the universe?
questions.answer: Because only Allah can make all these huge changes happen.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to show how easily Allah changes things?
questions.answer: It is like turning the pages of a book.

questions.question: What is one feeling this passage should give us about Allah?
questions.answer: Awe at His great power and beauty.

questions.question: What time of day is named in the target passage?
questions.answer: Nightfall, at ‘Isha time.

questions.question: What happens to the daylight still left in the sky?
questions.answer: It disappears.

questions.question: When night spreads over everything, what does that show about Allah?
questions.answer: It shows His power to control the world.

questions.question: What change in the year is used as another example of Allah’s control?
questions.answer: Summer changing into winter.

questions.question: What happens to the works of those who have passed away?
questions.answer: Their traces are wiped away with time.

questions.question: What does that wiping away remind us about life?
questions.answer: Life in this world ends, and there is another world after it.

questions.question: Does the passage teach that this world lasts forever or ends?
questions.answer: It teaches that this world ends.

questions.question: Does the passage teach that the next world is small and short or wide and lasting?
questions.answer: It is wide and lasting.

questions.question: According to the passage, who is the true Beloved and the One worshipped?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What is one sign that ‘Isha time has started?
questions.answer: The final light of daytime is gone.

questions.question: What fills the universe then?
questions.answer: Night.

questions.question: The passage mentions changing day into night. What does this help a reader understand about Allah?
questions.answer: Allah has complete power over creation.

questions.question: The passage also mentions changing summer into winter. What do both changes have in common?
questions.answer: Both show that Allah changes big things in an ordered way.

questions.question: What happens to signs left behind by people as years pass?
questions.answer: They disappear.

questions.question: What can a person infer from that about the dunya, this world?
questions.answer: It does not last forever.

questions.question: What future world is mentioned after the end of this one?
questions.answer: The hereafter.

questions.question: How does the passage compare Allah’s changing of worlds to something simple?
questions.answer: To turning pages in a book.

questions.question: What does that comparison teach about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: ‘Isha time reminds us that Allah changes all things, this world passes away, and the hereafter will come.

questions.question: Which two times of day are switched in the passage?
questions.answer: Day and night.

questions.question: Which two seasons are switched in the passage?
questions.answer: Summer and winter.

questions.question: Which two worlds are spoken about in the passage?
questions.answer: This world and the hereafter.

questions.question: What do all these changes show together?
questions.answer: They show Allah’s great power and rule.

questions.question: What happens to the marks left by people from the past?
questions.answer: Over time, they are removed.

questions.question: Who alone is described as the real Owner and Manager of the universe?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: What can Allah do with the world and the hereafter, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He can change from one to the other with ease.

questions.question: What should a Muslim remember at ‘Isha time from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah controls everything, this life is not forever, and we will return to Him.
